judgment_calls: Created separate heading-metadata nodes (n002, n007, n014, n021) for each rule's authority designation (system, root, root, user) rather than incorporating authority into the rule node itself. This follows the worked-example pattern where heading metadata becomes a separate node that rules need; however, these authority levels do not appear to be used within this span (no rule explicitly invokes or differs based on another rule's authority), so they may be dangling design elements or preparatory for phase U unwind with siblings.

Separated L1241 (hateful_content_educational_exception) as a distinct node (n016) from L1239 (hateful_content_prohibition, n015) to make the permission/exception explicit. Could have merged them into one rule node; separation clarifies that the exception is a distinct provision that can be independently needed by examples.

Treated 'protected_groups' as a dangling need (L1239 lists examples: race, religion, gender, sexual orientation, disability, etc., but does not formally define the set). The list provided is illustrative, not exhaustive. The formal definition likely appears elsewhere in the spec.

Kept 'disallowed_content_categories' as a dangling need throughout (n001, n008, n015, n022), as this is the inherited seed from phase D division. My span establishes one instance of it (sensitive_content_restrictions), but the three-tier framework itself is established earlier.
Treated 'objective_point_of_view' as a dangling need (referenced at L1157 and L1241 with link to #assume_objective_pov, indicating definition elsewhere). Appears to be a cross-document concept.
Treated 'transformation_exception' or 'transformation' as a dangling need (L1110 references it, but the span provides no definition of what counts as a transformation).
Treated 'usage_policies' as a dangling need (n004 references external URL openai.com/policies/usage-policies; not defined within document).
Each example block (n005-n006, n009-n013, n017-n020, n023-n025) is one single node per the brief rule; never decomposed the dialog inside a comparison block.

L1199's de-escalation guidance (n011) creates a new concept 'radicalization_vulnerability_deescalation' that is needed by the following example (n012). This is an intra-span cross-link within a single rule's elaboration.

No horizontal ordering established among the four rules (erotica/gore, extremism, hateful content, abuse). They appear as separate sections with different authority levels but no explicit precedence or conflict-resolution mechanism within my span. Any such ordering is a parent-level concern or a dangling need.
